All 23/23 pass against external URL. Real Claude calls verified (PONG, daily-brief narrative, weekly JSON, memory extraction).

minor.issue: On invalid token, server calls ws.close(code=4001) BEFORE ws.accept(). Starlette converts close-before-accept into an HTTP 403 handshake rejection, so the documented WS close code 4001 never reaches the client. Functionally rejection works. Fix: call await ws.accept() first, then await ws.close(code=4001).

Returns {ok:true} even when a non-owner calls it (silent no-op via owner_id filter on delete_one). Consider returning 403/404 to make ownership boundary explicit (same pattern as DELETE /projects flagged in iteration_1).
ok flag is True even when claude returns 'AI error: ...' as long as it does not start with that exact prefix. Tighter check (e.g., explicit PONG match) would catch silent provider failures.

Expires comparison uses datetime.fromisoformat without tz coercion; if stored expires_at is naive vs aware, the comparison silently falls into except branch and treats expired briefs as valid. Currently expires_at is always tz-aware (timedelta from datetime.now(timezone.utc)) so it works, but the except: pass swallows real errors too.
Persists every pattern returned by Claude with no dedupe; repeated calls cause memory bloat. Add hash-based dedupe or 'replace previous auto-extracted' semantics.

rca_of_the_issue: WS test originally failed expecting close code 4001 but received HTTP 403. RCA: server calls await ws.close(code=4001) without first awaiting ws.accept(). Starlette's WebSocket protocol implementation, when close is called pre-accept, denies the upgrade handshake itself with HTTP 403 rather than completing the handshake and then sending a close frame. Net behavior is identical from a security standpoint (connection refused) but the documented 4001 code is unreachable. Mitigation: in ws_endpoint, do `await ws.accept()` first, then on auth failure `await ws.close(code=4001)` so clients can read the close code.
